text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Over-the-counter market is ready to launch first trading session on September 27, Marcel Cobuz, vice-president of National Brokers' Association says in interview.
- Shimoda Australia Australian company which wanted to buy majority stake in Certinvest SA fund manager said two companies failed to reach cooperation accord.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Commodities exchanges in Bucharest and Constanta will hold tenders to sell 75,000 tonnes of scrap iron from rolling stock of national railway authority SNCFR.
- This year, CEC savings bank can offer subsidised credit rates for housing construction to 2,000 applicants.
ADEVARUL
- Privatisation is key for growth of tourism, a seminar in Bucharest showed.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romanian-South Korean carmaking venture Rodae SA will continue to build spare parts for Oltena cars, which Craiova plant used to make before going into partnership with Daewoo.
AZI
- Merrill Lynch International president will pay two-day visit to Romania starting Monday. He will meet National Bank governor and other Romanian officials.
ZIUA
- Trade balance gap has reached almost $1.0 billion.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) launched national reconciliation appeal at start of its electoral campaign for the November 3 parliamentary polls.
- Constitutional Court ruled that President Ion Iliescu's candidacy for a new term in the November 3 presidential polls is constitutional.
- Civic Alliance protests against constitutional court ruling, which says was made behind closed doors.
- Mircea Ionescu Quintus, head of National Liberal Party, (PNL) says in interview that Iliescu's candidacy violates the the constitution.
- Vasile Gionea, former head of the constitutional court, says in interview that Iliescu's candicacy is unconstitutional.
ADEVARUL
- "Romania turned into a market for powerful drugs", reads front-page headline presenting report on drugs consumption and smuggling.
- President Iliescu said he would not leave politics in case of defeat at the 1996 polls.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Report on Michael Jackson's concert due in Bucharest on September 14.
- Ethnic Hungarians to protest in western city of Timisoara on September 16 during signing ceremony of Hungarian-Romanian friendship treaty, said Reformist Bishop Laszlo Tokes.
- CDR presidential candidate Emil Constantinescu to sue ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) over breaking electoral law by attacking CDR's programme in TV clip.
- Newspaper presents ex-premier Petre Roman's political programme for the November presidential elections.
LIBERTATEA
- Bucharest schools with hygiene problems will not open on September 15 when new school year starts, to prevent spread of meningitis epidemic.
- Next parliament will have less MPs because Romania's population has decreased.
ZIUA
- Social Democratic Union (USD) of ex-premier Petre Roman to be admitted to Socialist International on Tuesday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) presidential candidate Gyorgy Frunda launched his programme for the November 3 polls. ($=3,176 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
